record.title: NP-hardness conjecture for recognizing generic-radii sphere-packing contact graphs
record.statement: A graph is a **generic-radii sphere-packing contact graph** if it is the contact graph of a sphere packing whose radii are generic. **NP-hardness conjecture.** Determining whether a graph is a generic-radii sphere-packing contact graph is NP-hard. The question is connected to recognizing penny graphs, and the source notes evidence for related NP-hardness results, but the stated problem remains unresolved.
record.source_name: Sean Dewar, “Identifying contact graphs of sphere packings with generic radii”, arXiv:2302.12588 (2024).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Extension of the main inequality to arbitrary total lifetimes
record.statement:
Let $(X_i(t))_{t\in[t_i]}$, for $i=1,\ldots,k$, be the discrete Markov chains considered in the paper, with total lifetime

$$
T:=\sum_{i=1}^k t_i.
$$

The total lifetime need not be even. **Lifespan-parity conjecture.** The inequality in the paper's main result holds for any total lifetime of the discrete Markov chains.

The conjecture removes the evenness assumption on the total lifetime. The source explains that this assumption is used only in the moment inequality, whose extension to odd total lifetime is left unresolved.

record.title: The vertex-deletion conjecture for correspondence packing number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $v\in V(G)$. **Vertex-deletion conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi_c^\star(G\setminus v)\ge \chi_c^\star(G)-2.
$$

Equivalently, adding a new vertex adjacent to all existing vertices increases the correspondence packing number by at most two. This would formalise the claim that no vertex contributes more than two to correspondence packing; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: The positroid Ehrhart-positivity conjecture
record.statement:
A matroid is **Ehrhart positive** if its associated base polytope has an Ehrhart polynomial whose coefficients are positive. A **positroid** is a matroid in the class of positroids introduced by Postnikov.

**Positroid Ehrhart-positivity conjecture.** Every positroid is Ehrhart positive.

The paper's result proves Ehrhart positivity for a certain class of panhandle matroids, which are positroids, and therefore supports this conjecture. The conjecture is attributed to the cited source and remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Daniel McGinnis, “Ehrhart positivity for a certain class of panhandle matroids”, arXiv:2303.04113 (2023).

record.title: Cooperative painting conjecture for systems of matroids
record.statement: Let $M_1,M_2,\ldots,M_t$ be a system of $k$-colorable matroids on the same ground set $E$. In round $i$, Ben chooses a subset $B_i\subseteq E$, and Ann colors a subset $A_i\subseteq B_i$ with color $i$ such that $A_i$ is independent in $M_i$. Each element $e\in E$ may be chosen at most $k$ times unless it is finally colored. Ann wins if the whole set $E$ is colored within at most $t$ rounds. If she has a winning strategy, the system has a **cooperative painting**. **Cooperative painting conjecture.** Every system of $k$-colorable matroids $M_1,M_2,\ldots,M_k$ on the set $E$ has a cooperative painting. This is posed as an open problem, extending analogous painting-game questions for graphs; the provided source does not state any resolution.
record.source_name: Tomasz Bartnicki, Sebastian Czerwiński, Jarosław Grytczuk and Zofia Miechowicz, “Cooperative coloring of matroids”, arXiv:2303.08776 (2023).

record.title: Vertex-transitivity conjecture for Šoltés graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $W(G)$ denote its Wiener index. A **Šoltés graph** is a graph for which deleting any vertex leaves the Wiener index unchanged. A graph is **vertex transitive** if its automorphism group acts transitively on its vertices. **Vertex-transitivity conjecture.** If $G$ is a Šoltés graph, then $G$ is vertex transitive. The motivation is that vertex deletion can produce equal Wiener indices on vertices in the same orbit, but the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Ryser's conjecture on rainbow cycle packings
record.statement:
Let $\vec{K}_n$ be the complete directed graph with both directed edges between every pair of vertices and a loop at every vertex, properly edge-coloured with $n$ colours. A **rainbow spanning subgraph** is one whose edges have distinct colours.

**Ryser's conjecture.** If $n$ is odd, then $\vec{K}_n$ contains a rainbow spanning subgraph in which every vertex has in-degree and out-degree equal to one. Equivalently, $\vec{K}_n$ can be packed with directed cycles in a rainbow fashion.

This is a conjecture about rainbow cycle decompositions of properly coloured complete directed graphs. The paper presents it as a famous open problem and discusses related strengthening by prescribing cycle lengths.
record.source_name: Alp Müyesser, “Cycle type in Hall-Paige: A proof of the Friedlander-Gordon-Tannenbaum conjecture”, arXiv:2303.16157 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16157

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2023). “The conjecture was confirmed by Wilcox , Evans , and Bray in 2009.”

record.title: The rainbow triangle-packing conjecture for properly coloured complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be a complete graph properly coloured with $n$ colours. A **rainbow subgraph** is one whose edges have pairwise distinct colours.

**Rainbow triangle-packing conjecture.** The graph $K_n$ contains a rainbow subgraph that is a disjoint union of triangles covering all but at most $C$ vertices, for some absolute constant $C$.

This is the triangle-length analogue of cycle-type questions for orthomorphisms and of rainbow Hamilton-cycle conjectures. The source does not give a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Good qubit LDPC codes yield good quantum LDPC rotor codes
record.statement:
Let $\phi_\infty(\mathcal{S})$ be a good qubit LDPC code, meaning that it has constant rate and relative distance. Let $p^*$ denote the parameter governing the local-dimension bound, and suppose that

$$
p^*<2\pi.
$$

**Rotor-code conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $\phi_\infty(\mathcal{S})$ represents a good quantum LDPC rotor code.

This conjecture proposes that the construction preserves goodness when imported from qubit stabilizer codes to rotor systems, whose two Pauli axes have local dimensions modeled by $\mathbb{R}_{2\pi}^{+}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$. The paper gives the construction under the stated bound but does not provide a proof that the resulting rotor code is good.
record.source_name: Lane G. Gunderman, “Stabilizer Codes with Exotic Local-dimensions”, arXiv:2303.17000 (2024).

record.title: Triangular realisation conjecture for graphical degree sequences
record.statement:
A **graphical degree sequence** is a finite sequence of nonnegative integers realised as the degree sequence of a finite simple graph. A graph is **triangular** if every edge belongs to a $3$-cycle.

**Triangular realisation conjecture.** Any graphical sequence all of whose terms are greater than or equal to $4$ admits a triangular realisation.

The conjecture proposes a degree threshold guaranteeing a realisation in which every edge lies in a triangle. The paper establishes the conjecture for a class of biregular graphical degree sequences, while the general case remains open.

record.title: The beta-conjecture for Gaussian-polynomial inequalities
record.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $0<a<b$, and let $\beta\geq1$. **The $\beta$-conjecture.** One has

$$
\binom{b+\beta a}{b}_q\geq\binom{a+\beta b}{a}_q,
$$

where the inequality is coefficientwise for polynomials in $q$. This is the three-parameter specialization of the preceding Gaussian inequality. The source says that the paper proves the case $\beta=2$, while the conjecture for general $\beta\geq1$ is left open there.
record.source_name: Tewodros Amdeberhan and David Callan, “Gaussian inequality”, arXiv:2304.03395 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03395

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

record.title: A coefficientwise Gaussian-polynomial product inequality
record.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $0\leq k\leq a<b$. **The codicil conjecture.** The following equivalent-looking coefficientwise inequalities hold:

$$
\binom{a}{k}_q\binom{a+b}{b-k}_q\geq\binom{b}{k}_q\binom{a+b}{a-k}_q,
$$

or

$$
\binom{a}{k}_q\binom{b}{k}_q\binom{b+a}{b}_q\left[\frac{1}{\binom{a+k}{k}_q}-\frac{1}{\binom{b+k}{k}_q}\right]\geq0.
$$

Here $\binom{n}{k}_q$ denotes the Gaussian polynomial and $\geq$ denotes coefficientwise comparison. The source presents this as a codicil arising from calculations related to the $\beta$-conjecture; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Tewodros Amdeberhan and David Callan, “Gaussian inequality”, arXiv:2304.03395 (2023).

record.title: Heng's NMDS code conjecture for the extended trace code
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let

$$
\mu_{q+1}=\{x\in \mathbb{F}_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\},\qquad D=\mu_{q+1}\setminus\{-1\},
$$

and let $\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q:\mathbb{F}_{q^2}\to\mathbb{F}_q$ be the trace map, $\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q(x)=x+x^q$. For $b\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ and $c\in\mathbb{F}_q$, define

$$
c(b,c)=\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q(bx+b)+c)_{x\in D},-\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q(b)\bigr),
$$

and set

$$
\widetilde{\overline{C_D}}=\{c(b,c):b\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2},\ c\in\mathbb{F}_q\}.
$$

**Heng's conjecture.** If $q>2$, then $\widetilde{\overline{C_D}}$ is a $[q+1,3,q-2]_q$ NMDS code.
This conjecture concerns the remaining family of NMDS codes identified by Heng; proving it establishes the asserted parameters and the NMDS property for this extended trace construction.

record.title: The perfect Martin sequence conjecture for cyclically 4-connected 3-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graphs with the same number of vertices, and let $v_1$ and $v_2$ be vertices whose deletion produces periods $\mathcal{P}(G_1\setminus v_1)$ and $\mathcal{P}(G_2\setminus v_2)$. Define the Martin sequence by

$$
\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^{\bullet})=\left(\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^{[2]}),\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^{[4]}),\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^{[6]}),\ldots\right).
$$

**Perfect Martin sequence conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{P}(G_1\setminus v_1)=\mathcal{P}(G_2\setminus v_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G_1^{\bullet})=\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G_2^{\bullet}).
$$

Available data is compatible with this purely combinatorial characterization of equal periods, but the general assertion remains unproved.
record.source_name: Erik Panzer and Karen Yeats, “Feynman symmetries of the Martin and c_2 invariants of regular graphs”, arXiv:2304.05299 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05299

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

record.title: Azevedo–Shumyatsky conciseness conjecture for commutators of non-commutator words
record.statement:
Let $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ be non-commutator words in pairwise disjoint sets of variables. For a group word $v=v(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$, write $v(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ for the word obtained by substituting the $u_i$ into $v$. A word is **concise** if, in every group, finiteness of its set of values implies finiteness of its verbal subgroup.

**Azevedo–Shumyatsky conjecture.** The word

$$
\gamma_r(u_1,\ldots,u_r)=[u_1,\ldots,u_r]
$$

is concise.

This conjecture generalizes known conciseness results for commutators involving non-commutator words; the paper's abstract states that it proves this generalized conjecture for lower central and derived words.
record.source_name: Gustavo A. Fernández-Alcober and Matteo Pintonello, “Conciseness on normal subgroups and new concise words from lower central and derived words”, arXiv:2304.06380 (2023).

record.title: Injectivity of the integer point transform without dilation
record.statement:
Let $d4ab,d4ac\binom{}{}$ be rational polytopes in $d4ad^d$, and let $d709^*$ be the vector specified in the paper's algebraic-independence condition.

**Integer point transform injectivity conjecture.** If

$$
\sigma_{\mathcal{P}}(\xi^*)=\sigma_{\mathcal{Q}}(\xi^*)
$$

then $d4ab=d4ac$.

This would strengthen the stated main theorem by eliminating the dilation factor $k$, making evaluation of the integer point transform at the single vector $d709^*$ a complete invariant for rational polytopes. The source presents this as an open question.

record.title: Tomon’s shifting conjecture for $(r,t)$-maximal families
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal G\subset 2^{[n]}$ be an **$(r,t)$-maximal family**, meaning a family maximal with respect to the relevant $(r,t)$-intersection property, and let $\mathcal H$ be a shifted family obtained from $\mathcal G$ by shifting. For $i=0,1,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{r}\right\rfloor$, define

$$
\mathcal F_i^t(r)=\{F\subset[n]:|F\cap[t+ri]|\geq t+(r-1)i\}.
$$

**Tomon’s conjecture.** If $\mathcal H\subset\mathcal F_i^t(r)$, then

$$
\mathcal G\cong\mathcal F_i^t(r).
$$

The conjecture would generalize the lemma used in the paper and is proposed as a route toward stability results for $r$-wise $t$-intersecting families.

record.title: Arbitrarily deep failure of log-concavity for independence polynomials of trees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a tree, let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number, and write its independence polynomial as

$$
I(G;x)=\sum_{j=0}^{\alpha(G)}i_jx^j.
$$

Here, log-concavity at the $j$th coefficient means $i_j^2\geq i_{j-1}i_{j+1}$. **Arbitrarily deep failure conjecture.** Log-concavity may fail at the coefficient indexed by $\alpha(G)-k$ for arbitrarily chosen $k\in\{1,2,\ldots,\alpha(G)-1\}$. This is motivated by an explicit tree whose failure occurs at the $\alpha(G)-2$ coefficient; the supplied text does not state whether the proposed extension has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Ohr Kadrawi and Vadim E. Levit, “The independence polynomial of trees is not always log-concave starting from order 26”, arXiv:2305.01784 (2023).

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023). “However, in the same year, Kadrawi, Levit, Yosef, and Mizrachi found a number of counterexamples to the log-concavity conjecture in .”

record.title: Pak–Panova's unary Littlewood–Richardson completeness conjecture
record.statement:
For partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu$, let $\textsf{ComputeLR}$ be the problem whose input is $\lambda,\mu,\nu$ encoded in unary and whose output is the Littlewood–Richardson coefficient $c^{\lambda}_{\mu\nu}$. Here unary encoding writes each part using a number of symbols proportional to its value.

**Pak–Panova's conjecture.** When the input is in unary, $\textsf{ComputeLR}$ is $\#\mathrm{P}$-complete.

For binary input, the source recalls Narayanan's $\#\mathrm{P}$-completeness theorem, whereas the unary case was presented as unresolved. The conjecture asserts that unary encoding does not make the counting problem easier.
